newsitem.title: CHILE: Quebrada Blanca union doubts output at 50 pct.
newsitem.headline: Quebrada Blanca union doubts output at 50 pct.

text.p: Quebrada Blanca's striking union said Wednesday it doubted the management's assertion that the mine was producing about 50 percent of its usual cathode output.

Talks to end the week-old strike have come to a dead stop, and the government's local labor relations board told the union it may intervene to prod both sides to return to the negotiating table, said union president Nelson Fuentes.
He said he doubted that the mine, owned by Canada's Cominco Ltd, was managing to keep up production of about 100 tonnes of electrowon cathodes a day, as general manager James Drake said Tuesday.

"Even when we're all working, we're producing at about 80 percent of design capacity of 216 tonnes a day, so I doubt that they're keeping up 50 percent capacity with untrained personnel in the plant," Fuentes told Reuters.
"This equipment also needs daily maintenance and I don't know how they're going to do that without trained personnel," said Fuentes, who said he works in the electrowinning sector.

Drake said that despite the strike by 70 percent of workforce, the mine was producing cathodes at about 50 percent its usual rate, or about 100 tonnes of cathodes a day. Located in the Atacama desert near the Bolivian border, the mine produces some 75,000 tonnes of copper a year.
Drake said the mine could keep up with delivery commitments for the moment, thanks in part to inventory stocks which he said would last a few weeks.

Both he and Fuentes said no date was set for new wage talks, after they broke down over the weekend. About 350 workers walked off the job last Wednesday after their wage contract expired without a renewal.

Talks foundered on union demands for a special bonus to compensate for the high altitude of the site, at 4,200 meters above sea level, over and above the "isolation bonus" which the mine already pays to compensate for the site's remoteness and altitude.

In contrast to the angry rhetoric that often characterizes wage talks in Chilean mining, Fuentes said talks with Quebrada Blanca management were conducted in "a cordial atmosphere, one of mutual respect and understanding."

"But unfortunately we have tripped up on this one detail (the altitude bonus). We should have been able to finish these negotiations without a strike, and I hope in the future we will be able to negotiate without reaching this extreme," he said.
